text: Mr. Alvarez, a retired teacher, sat at his kitchen table with his tablet. 'Plan my dinners for Monday to Friday,' he told the assistant. 'Start with fish on Monday, and then email the plan to my daughter.' The assistant made a five-day dinner plan and got ready to send it to his daughter Lucia. Then Mr. Alvarez remembered something. 'Wait, not fish on Monday. Make it chicken. Lucia does not like fish.' The assistant changed Monday from fish to chicken and said so out loud. It also put a big pot of vegetable soup on Wednesday, because he wanted one easy night. Mr. Alvarez said the pot was as heavy as a stone, but he liked it. The assistant said the plan was ready, and it sent the email with the new list to Lucia. He smiled. His week of meals was done.

A weather forecast tells you what the sky will probably do, so you can plan your day. Each morning, many people ask their phone or speaker for it. They can change the place, the day, or the kind of news they want. You might say, What's the weather in Leeds on Saturday? Or, Will it rain this afternoon? If you want to know what to wear, you can ask, Do I need a coat today? or How cold is it outside? Some people ask for a warning, like Tell me if it will rain, so they do not forget their umbrella. Others plan a trip and ask, Will it be sunny when I pick pears on Sunday? A forecast is only a good guess, but it gets better the closer the day comes.

Priya was waiting for the bus and texting her phone assistant. She typed, Hello, could you please tune the radio app to the local news station, because my grandfather says there is a traffic problem near our school and I want to know if the bus will be late? The assistant understood that she wanted two things: the news station, and the traffic report. It opened the radio app, found the station, and started playing it. For the first moment she heard only music. She swiped the screen to turn the sound up, and soon a man began to read the news. The assistant told her the traffic report would come at ten past the hour. Priya asked it to remind her, and it set a reminder for ten past.

Someone wants a taxi to come to their home soon.
Get me a cab.
I need a ride from my house in ten minutes.
Can a car pick me up at the corner? Not at the main door.
Send a taxi, please, but not a big van.
My dad and I need to get to the station, and we will split the cost.
Book me a ride, and do not pick the cheapest one, because the last driver was rude and bitter.
Is there a car nearby that can take me to the airport?
I would be very grateful if you could arrange a ride for half past six this evening.

Tom was a busy parent with a full day ahead. His hands were covered in cake mix for his daughter's birthday party, so he spoke to his phone. 'Call my mother on speaker. Do not leave a voicemail if she does not answer, because I will try again later.' The assistant understood. It called his mother and turned on the speaker, so Tom could keep mixing. The phone rang and rang. Tom said, 'Don't hang up too soon, she is slow to get to the phone.' The assistant let it ring a long time, but nobody answered. It told him that his mother did not pick up and that it had left no voicemail, just as he asked. Tom nodded and put the cake in the oven.

Mrs. Okafor owned a small shop, and she wanted to take her helpers out for dinner. She had heard good things about an Italian place near the shop. 'Find that restaurant and book a table for twenty-five people on Friday at seven,' she told her phone. The assistant found the restaurant and looked at the booking page. It said large groups needed a manual check by the staff, so the assistant could not book the table by itself. Instead, it sent a request for twenty-five people at seven on Friday and told Mrs. Okafor that the staff would reply soon. While she waited, she went back to the jigsaw puzzle on her counter. An hour later, the restaurant said yes, and the assistant told her the table was hers.

When you book a ride, the app needs to know where you are and where you want to go. Then it finds a driver and tells you when the car will arrive. People change the pickup point and the time a lot. They say, Pick me up at the park gate, or Come to the back door, or Make it twenty minutes later. If the car is late, they ask, Where is my driver? Someone going to the recycling center with old boxes may ask for a car with a big trunk. A good assistant should understand that Make it later and Come in ten minutes both change the pickup time. Drivers are often proud of a clean car, and riders like to know what kind of car is coming.

name: turn_on_subtitles
does: Shows words on the screen for what the actors say, and picks the language and the size of the words.
inputs: the show or screen, on or off, and the language
people say:
- I can't hear the actors, show me the words
- The baby is asleep, so keep the sound off and put the text on
- The voices are so rough and mumbly, I can't follow
- The actors whisper too much, can you show captions
- My dog's leash is in one hand and the remote is lost, put words on the screen in Spanish

Person: Morning. Move my dentist appointment to tomorrow at seven.
Assistant: Do you mean seven in the morning or seven in the evening?
Person: Evening. Sorry, my head is still foggy. It is so cold in here and the light is too bright.
Assistant: No problem. I moved the dentist to tomorrow at seven in the evening. Can I help with anything else?
Person: Is Dana free then?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can only see your calendar, not Dana's. You could send her a message to ask.
Person: Okay, I will do that after coffee. Thanks.

name: warm_up_room
does: Uses the home network to turn up the heat in one room to a chosen temperature by a chosen time.
inputs: the room, the temperature, and the time
people say:
- It's freezing in the bedroom
- I came in with wet boots and my feet are like ice
- Have the living room cozy by six
- Get the bathroom warm before my shower
- The temperature will drop tonight, so heat up the hall

Jun had just moved to the city, and it was a cold morning, so he wore his thick coat to the market. He was still learning to translate prices in his head, so he took out his phone and typed in a hurry: wat is 48 times 3, then plus 15. The assistant understood that he wanted 48 multiplied by three, and then fifteen added to the answer. It said the answer was 159. Jun was buying three scarves for his new flat, and each one cost 48, plus a small bag for 15. He thanked the assistant, paid the seller, and put the scarves in his bag. Then he walked home through the busy streets, happy that he knew the right total.

Person: clean the flor
Assistant: Which room should the robot vacuum clean, the kitchen or the living room?
Person: kitchen. a cake fell on the floor and there are crumbs everywhere
Assistant: Oh no, I'm sorry about the cake. I will send the vacuum to the kitchen now. Should it mop too?
Person: no, i don't know how that works, just vacuum
Assistant: Okay, vacuum only. It will go back to its dock and stay away from the kitchen when it is done.

A cycling app records your rides: how far you went, how fast you were, and which route you took. It is for seeing how you are getting better and for planning your next trip. People change the goal or the route as they go. They say, Update my goal to fifty kilometers this week, or Show me a flatter route. On a rare sunny day off, someone may ask for a longer loop. Others ask, How fast was I yesterday? or Stop recording, I am at the cafe. Some friends turn it into a game and compare who rode the most. After a ride, you can say, Save this trip, and the app keeps it.

Recipes, shops and roads use different units, so people often need to change one into another. A cook may find a fancy recipe from another country that lists grams, while the kitchen scale shows ounces. Someone buying rice may see kilos on the bag but want pounds. People ask, How many cups is 200 grams of rice? or Give me that in ounces, please. Others say, I like Celsius, so tell me the oven heat that way. Runners ask how many miles are in ten kilometers. The helper does the sum and says the new number with its unit, so the cook knows exactly how much to weigh out.

Water comes into your home through a pipe, and a meter counts how much you use. The water heater keeps some of it hot, so you can have a warm shower. A small leak can waste a lot of water, so people want quick news about it. They say, Tell me if the water runs all night, or Why is my water bill so high? Some people change the heat: Make the water hotter, or Turn the heater down while we are away. A grandma who loves long baths may say, Warm the tank by evening. When the pipes are fine, the helper just says nothing is wrong.

A student wants to know what homework is due tomorrow.
whats due tomorow
What homework do I have for tomorrow?
Anything due soon?
I have a cold and missed class, so tell me what I need to hand in.
List my assignments by date.
Did the teacher shift the science deadline?
I am sleepy, so just say which task I should finish first.
Could you please tell me everything I still need to turn in this week, so that I can plan my evenings?
Show me tomorrow's schoolwork.

Rosa, a gardener, came in from the garden with dirt on her hands. Her dog Pepper stood by his empty bowl and looked at her. 'Pepper looks thirsty, and his bowl is bone dry,' Rosa said to the speaker. The assistant understood that she wanted the water bowl filled. It turned on the pet fountain in the kitchen, and fresh water began to flow. Rosa also said she had to drive to the gym at six. The assistant offered to remind her to take Pepper for a walk before then, and she said yes. It set the reminder for five o'clock. Pepper drank his water, wagged his tail, and went to find his favorite ball.

Kai was in his room, texting the home assistant. 'Dude, it's too hot up here. Can you make it two degrees cooler and run the fan twice as fast?' The house had started to fill with heat after dinner, because his dad had cooked beef stew all afternoon. The assistant understood that Kai wanted the air conditioning lowered by two degrees and the fan made faster. It did both, and it told him the new setting was 22 degrees. Kai asked if that was a total of two degrees lower than before, and the assistant said yes. After ten minutes, the room felt fresh, and Kai went back to his game.

In August, the weather can change fast, so many people check it often. A forecast tells you the heat, the wind, and the chance of rain. It is meant to help you choose what to do and what to wear. You may notice a round sun symbol on a clear day and a gray cloud on a rainy one. People change the place and the time: What will it be like in Rome on Friday? or Check this weekend. They also ask for alerts, like Tell me if it will storm tonight. Or they ask about clothes: Should I take a jacket? Each answer helps them be ready.

A calendar helps you remember what you plan to do and when. You can put in meetings, birthdays, and free time. Most of the time, you ask to add, move, or remove things. Someone says, Put lunch with Sam on Thursday at noon, or Move my meeting to later, or Cancel Friday's class. Others ask, Am I free on Monday afternoon? A light week might have only one event on it. Before a trip, a person may add, Pack bags at six, and a note to buy an apple for the road. When your plans change, you just tell the calendar the new day or time, and it keeps everything in order.

A cook wants a recipe made for six people instead of four.
Make this serve six.
Scale it up for six people, but don't change the cooking time.
I'm cooking for my friend the nurse and four others, so adjust the amounts.
Bump the recipe up to six portions.
Increase everything by half.
Don't give me cups, only grams, for six people.
Please rewrite the list at the bottom of the page for six, because I want a dish to brighten up the party table and I do not want to run out.

Ben was eight, and he was baking cookies with his mom. The baking sheet was already in the oven, and he wanted to know when to take it out. He typed to the speaker in a hurry: set a timr for twelve minutes and make it sing. The assistant understood that Ben wanted a twelve-minute timer. It said it could not sing, but it could make a happy bell sound, and Ben said that was fine. It was strange to wait so quietly, so he watched the oven light. When the twelve minutes were up, the bell rang. Ben shouted, 'Cookies!' and his mom took out the sheet with big oven gloves.

Babies need food and sleep at regular times, and parents often use a digital helper to keep track. A feeding reminder tells you when the last bottle was and when the next one is due. A nap timer shows how long the baby has slept. A baby monitor lets you hear or see the room from far away. Parents change things by saying, Remind me to feed the baby at three, or Start the nap timer, or Turn the monitor up. In autumn, when evenings come early, they may say, Dim the nursery light at six. If the baby stirs, the monitor sends a message to the phone.

name: night_check
does: Looks at the cameras, doors, and windows each night and gives a short report on anything open or moving.
inputs: the time of the check, and which rooms to include
people say:
- Is the house safe before I go to bed?
- Did I lock up?
- Arrange a look at all the doors at ten
- Did anything odd happen in the middle of the night?
- Make sure the garage is shut

Assistant: I'm sorry, that lamp only makes white light, so I can't make it blue. Shall I keep it on bright white?
Person: ok fine. thanks

Dana, a nurse, came home after a night shift, tired and sore. The hot tub on the patio looked cold and gray in the morning light. 'The hot tub is freezing and I really need to soak,' she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted warm water. It turned on the heater and set the water to 38 degrees. It told her the tub would be ready in about an hour. Dana put the kettle on the stove and made some tea while she waited. She also asked the assistant to write the filter check on her main list, so she would not forget it. The assistant added it for the weekend. An hour later, the water was warm.

A home security system watches your house when you are away. Cameras record, sensors notice when doors or windows open, and an alarm sings out loudly if something is wrong. The price depends on how many parts you want. No system is perfect, so people check on it often. They say, Is the front door locked? or Turn on the alarm, I am leaving. They ask to see a camera: Show me the back yard. Or they ask for news: Tell me if someone comes to the door. Some people need quiet after a false alarm and say, Turn it off, it was just me.

Leo woke up on Sunday morning and reached for his phone. He typed fast: what moovies are on near me tonight. The assistant understood that he wanted cinema times for films showing that evening. It found three cinemas close by and read the times out loud. There was a single showing of the dog film at eight. Leo remembered that the trailer had a dog with a red collar, and he had paused it the night before. He asked the assistant to continue the trailer where he stopped. It did, and the little dog ran across the screen again. Leo laughed, and the assistant asked if he wanted it to save the eight o'clock time. He said yes.

A coffee machine, a kettle, and an oven all do one job: they heat something. A smart kitchen helper lets you control them with your voice. People change the time or the heat. They say, Heat the oven to 180, or Boil the kettle, or Make a strong coffee. Some tasks are difficult to remember, like the dishwasher, so people say, Tell me when the dishes are done. When you bake, you can follow your nose, but a timer helps more. Some machines can email you or send a message when a job is finished, so you do not need to stand next to them.

Hector drove a bus at night and slept in the daytime. One afternoon, he lay down with a sour taste of coffee still in his mouth. 'Wake me at four,' he told the speaker. Then he thought for a moment. 'No, wait, make it five. My grandma comes at six, and I want an hour to clear the kitchen first.' The assistant understood that Hector was fixing the time. It cancelled the alarm for four and set a new one for five, and it told him plainly that it had made the change. Hector said thanks, closed his eyes, and fell asleep.

Marco, a cook, was planning a party for his sister. His hands were full of flour, so he talked to the speaker. 'Guest list,' he said. The assistant opened the party guest list and read out the twelve names. 'Sort names,' Marco said next. The assistant put the names in order from A to Z and said so. Marco wanted a calm mood in the room, so he said, 'Soft music.' The assistant played some gentle piano songs. Marco smiled, put a plant on the table, and went back to his dough. He liked that he only needed two words each time, and the assistant always understood what he meant.

Person: Did my parcel come?
Assistant: I see two parcels on the way. Which one do you mean, the books or the lamp?
Person: The books. Is it more than one box? I saw a flash of the van outside.
Assistant: Yes, the books are in two boxes, and the van stopped at your street a minute ago.
Person: Can you tell the driver to leave them on the porch? My mailbox is messy and it hasn't got enough depth for a box.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't talk to the driver or change the delivery. I can remind you when the boxes are marked as delivered.
Person: Okay, please do that.

name: read_aloud
does: Reads text from a page, a letter, or a message out loud in a clear voice at the speed you choose.
inputs: what to read, and how slow or fast
people say:
- My eyes are tired, can you read this to me?
- Say that message out loud, slowly
- I can't see the small print on the cereal box, what does it say?
- Go straight to the last paragraph and read it
- My eyes water when I look at the screen too long, so speak the page for me

Sana had just moved to the city, and her new job sent her an invoice in a language she did not know well. The page took a long time to load on her phone, and then she saw a line with words she could not read. She said to her assistant, 'Please translate minimum payment into French and show me how to spell it.' The assistant understood that she wanted two things at once: a translation and the spelling. It said the words were paiement minimum, and it spelled them out one letter at a time. Sana wrote them down in her notebook. She felt proud, because she could now find the right line on the invoice.

name: gift_idea_finder

inputs: who the gift is for, what they enjoy, and a budget
people say:

- I need something fast, the party is tomorrow
- Any ideas for a ten year old who loves space?
- Help, I have twenty dollars and no clue

Person: Record a video.
Assistant: Sure. Which camera should I use, the one in the hallway or the one in the kitchen?
Person: Hallway. I wonder if the cat does her morning run again.
Assistant: Okay. How long should I record?
Person: Twice as long as yesterday.
Assistant: Yesterday's clip was five minutes, so I will record ten. Do you want to share it afterwards?
Person: Yes, send it to my sister. That cat is her favourite.

A bill tells you how much you owe for something like electricity, water, or rent, and when it must be paid. Paying on time avoids angry letters and extra fees. People keep track of due dates so they do not forget. They say, When is my electric bill due? or Remind me to pay rent on the first, or Pay the water bill on Friday. Bills often climb in winter, so someone may ask, Why did it go up this month? Each month, a family may set money aside, just like they buy grapes every week, so that the bills never come as a surprise.

Grandpa Joe wanted to cook his mother's soup for his young grandson. He did not know all the steps by heart, so he took out his phone and typed in a hurry: how long do i boil the potatos for soup. The assistant understood that he wanted the boiling time. It said about twenty minutes, until the potatoes are soft when you poke them with a fork. Grandpa Joe said, 'Good, now I'm saving this recipe so I never lose it.' The assistant saved the steps in his favorites list and told him where to find them. The soup smelled wonderful, and the boy ate two bowls.

name: repeat_order
does: Sets up a weekly food order that is sent by itself, so the same meal arrives at the same time each week.
inputs: the restaurant, the meal, and the day and time
people say:
- Get me pizza every Friday at six
- The kids want their usual dinner again
- Same as last time, but every week
- Write down my order for each Tuesday and don't ask me again
- Stop me from picking dinner over and over

Wind and rain depend on where you are, so a forecast always starts with a place. The south of a country is often warmer, so a trip there needs different clothes. People ask for a forecast and then change it: Show me the south coast, or Zoom in on my town, or What about next Tuesday? Before walking the dog, someone may ask, Will it rain in the next hour? Rain maps let you zoom in until you can see your own street. People also ask for more or less detail, like Just tell me hot or cold, or Give me the wind speed too.

Nina was an office worker, and she was working late on a budget for her team. Her boss wanted to raise the money for the kitchen, including a new stove. Nina looked at her numbers and said to her assistant, 'Add 340 and 275, and then tell me what half of that is.' The assistant understood that she wanted two answers in a row. First, it said the sum was 615. Then it said half of 615 was 307.5. Nina wrote both numbers in her sheet. She thanked the assistant and sent the budget to her boss before the end of the day.

Grandma Ruth sat on the porch on a chilly afternoon with a book and a blanket. She said to her tablet, 'Could you please set a timer for twenty-five minutes of reading, and then a five-minute break, because my doctor says I should rest my eyes and I always forget?' The assistant understood that she wanted a focus timer followed by a short break. It set both and told her plainly what it had done. Ruth also said she had to drive to the shop at five, and the assistant added a reminder. When the first timer rang, a woman walking by waved at her, and Ruth waved back and rested her eyes.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap, and spinning. A dial or an app sets the heat, the spin, and the time. People change these things by saying, Wash on cold, or Make it quicker, or Spin it slower. A number on the machine shows how many minutes are left. Dryers spend more energy than washers, so many people dry less and hang clothes instead. If you see a weird stain, you can ask, How do I get this stain out? Some people ask for a message when the wash is done: Tell me when the laundry is finished, and then they can fold it before it wrinkles.

Omar had just moved to the city and could not work out his oven. The paper manual was a document in another language, and he did not want to read all of it. He was upstairs and the kitchen was downstairs, so he called out to the speaker, 'Make the oven hotter, by about twenty degrees.' The assistant understood that Omar wanted the heat raised. The oven was at 180, so it set it to 200 and said so. Omar decided to bake bread that night, so he asked for a timer of thirty minutes too. The assistant started it. Omar went downstairs, and the whole house soon smelled warm and good.

Mr. Chen owned a pepper and spice shop, and he was very busy. His customers called out from the counter asking about the City game. He said to his phone, 'Could you please tell me the score of the City match, and if it is not over, tell me when it ends, because I want to close early and I need enough time to get home before the crowd?' The assistant understood that he wanted the score and the end time. It said City was winning two to one with ten minutes left. Mr. Chen told his customers the news, and they cheered. The assistant told him again when the match was over.

Lena, a student, woke up when the power went out in her building. It was dark and quiet. She found her flashlight, an important item, and said to her phone, 'Excuse me, could you please tell me if there is a power cut in my area and when it will end, because my flatmates are out and my phone battery is getting low?' The assistant checked and said that there was planned work on her street. The power would come back at ten o'clock. Lena stirred her soup on the gas stove, and ate it in the light of the flashlight. She was glad that her electricity bill was already paid, and she waited for the lights to come back.
